PE1-11.hint: Compare with \(y = A\sin(B(x - C)) + D\). The amplitude is \(|A|\), the period is \(\dfrac{2\pi}{B}\), and the midline is \(y = D\). For the phase shift, factor \(B\) out of the parentheses first.
slips: Reading the phase shift as \(\pi\) in (a). Factor out the \(4\): the shift is \(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\).
Calling the amplitude \(-1\) in (b). Amplitude is never negative; the minus sign is a reflection.
Using \(B = 3\) in (b). The coefficient of \(x\) is \(\dfrac{1}{3}\), so the period is \(2\pi \div \dfrac{1}{3}\).

PE1-12.hint: The amplitude is the height of the peak above the midline. A peak and the very next trough are half a period apart.
slips: Using the distance \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\) as the full period. It is only half.
Giving the amplitude as \(6\), the distance from the peak to the trough.
PE1-12.source: Practice Exam 1 review (the 38 questions on the Exam 1 review site, 172exam1review)

items.stem: For each function, identify the amplitude, period, midline, and phase shift.

parts.a: Amplitude \(2\); period \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\); midline \(y = 3\); phase shift \(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\) to the right, because \(4x - \pi = 4\left(x - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\).
Amplitude \(1\); period \(6\pi\); midline \(y = -4\); phase shift \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\) to the left, because \(\dfrac{1}{3}x + \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\).

items.stem: A sinusoidal wave \(y = A\sin(Bx)\), with \(A \gt  0\) and \(B \gt  0\), has a peak at \(\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}, 3\right)\) and the next trough at \(\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{4}, -3\right)\).

parts.a: Amplitude \(= 3\). A peak to the next trough is half a period: \(\dfrac{3\pi}{4} - \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} = \dfrac{T}{2}\), so \(T = \pi\).
